To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL‐6‐/− mice develop obesity‐induce renal impairment.

IL‐6‐/− mice develop obesity‐induce renal dysfunction, and this phenotype is associated with increased renal expression of the pro‐inflammatory chemokine CCL2, and increased renal expression of IL‐6, which is regulated by CCL2.

IL‐6‐/ mice develop obesity‐induce renal impairment, which is associated with increased oxidative stress, inflammation and apoptosis in the kidney, and that IL‐6 is involved in the regulation of renal function in obesity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the role of the immune system in obesity and its related complications, including insulin resistance, inflammation, and cancer.
the study of the effects of the IL-6 on obesity and obesity-induced renal impairment.
the role of the IL-6 cytokine in the development of obesity-related renal disease and its potential as a therapeutic target.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL‐6‐/ ‐ mice are protected from obesity‐induced kidney injury and inflammation.
